newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 25.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Labour puts McKinnon as PM: Talk that National deputy leader Don McKinnon will oust Prime Minister Jim Bolger resurfaced in Parliament on Tuesday. Page 2.

Peters backs PM's surplus explanation: Treasurer Winston Peters on Tuesday backed Prime Minister Jim Bolger's claim that the resumption of tax cuts from July 1998 was one reason for the lower surplus forecast for the coming financial year. Page 2.

Call for petrol cut as crude oil becomes cheaper: The Automobile Association and Consumers Institute say petrol companies should be moving faster to bring down petrol prices in New Zealand after recent falls in international crude oil prices. Page 18.

Mortgage interest easing won't be big -- economists: Beneath the rhetoric of the government's Budget tomorrow and the Reserve Bank's monetary policy statement on Friday there would be at most a small fall in mortgage rates, economists said. Page 18.
GPG stands to make $3.8m profit: Guinness Peat Group stands to make a $3.8 million profit from building sales after its raid on Turners and Growers two years ago. Page 18.
Statistics show beer output down: Beer output fell to its lowest level in 27 years in the year to March, Statistics NZ said on Tuesday. Page 19.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Southern power companies to compete for home customers: Two South Island power companies are to trial a technique called profiling which is designed to bring competition within reach of residential electricity consumers.
Winston's 'wait for it' has hope riding high: By far the most important test of Thursday's budget is what it will mean for economic growth and hence jobs and living standards.
Tax take to slow debt task: A lower tax take and higher spending will dramatically slow the government's debt repayment programme for the next three years, economists say.
An ATM at home: People might eventually have an automatic teller machine in their own home if a new product takes off.

Phillips defends 'informal meetings': The Former Pacer Kerridge executive chairman David Phillips began his day in court on Tuesday on $13.6 million of fraud charges by criticising New Zealand Herald coverage of his evidence.
THE PRESS
Police close Chch drug 'shops': Police on Tuesday shut down drug-dealing "shops" throughout Christchurch in an operation targeting the Black Power gang's criminal enterprises. Page 1.
School leaving age stays at 16: The school leaving age would remain at 16 next year, rather than rising, Education Minister Wyatt Creech said on Tuesday. Page 2.

Sowry rejects housing link: Social Welfare Minister Roger Sowry says it is wrong to link the sale of 52 surplus Social Welfare family homes with a damning report from the Commissioner of Children over the lack of beds for young offenders. Page 7.

Tax losses seen as key to Cry TV bid: The foiled attempt to keep Cry TV Ltd out of liquidation may have been a bid by the company principals and associates to take advantage of tax losses as major creditors. Page 24.

Telstra tells Telecom subsidiary to pay: Australian telecommunications company Telstra has told Pacific Star, Telecom's loss-making Australian subsidiary, that services will be stopped unless it makes payment for alleged debts. Page 26.
